diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

helm_release.karpenter already implicitly depends on module.karpenter because its `values` template references `module.karpenter.service_account` and `module.karpenter.queue_name`. The explicit `depends_on = [module.karpenter]` entry duplicates that dependency and can be removed.

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class already implicitly depends on module.eks: its `triggers` reference module.eks.cluster_primary_security_group_id and module.eks.cluster_security_group_id. The explicit `depends_on` entry for module.eks is redundant.

null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class already implicitly depends on module.karpenter: its `triggers` reference module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn. The explicit `depends_on` entry for module.karpenter is redundant.
null_resource.update_kubeconfig already implicitly depends on module.eks: its local-exec command interpolates module.eks.cluster_name. The explicit `depends_on = [module.eks]` is redundant.

null_resource.delete_daemonset deletes the aws-node (VPC CNI) DaemonSet, which should only happen once Calico has been installed so a new CNI is in place. It currently depends only on module.eks and null_resource.update_kubeconfig, so nothing guarantees null_resource.create_calico_installation has run first — deleting the CNI beforehand leaves nodes without pod networking. Add a dependency on null_resource.create_calico_installation.
